questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: ISRO's GSLV-F18 mission on 30 October 2026 placed the NVS-03 navigation satellite into which initial orbit, supporting which Indian system?
options: A geosynchronous transfer orbit for NavIC
A sun-synchronous orbit for ocean-colour imaging
A low Earth orbit for crewed spaceflight
A lunar transfer orbit for deep-space science
explanations: Correct — the official mission note says NVS-03 was injected into a geosynchronous transfer orbit and is part of the next-generation NavIC constellation.
Incorrect — the mission was a navigation-satellite launch, not an ocean-colour imaging mission.
Incorrect — NVS-03 is not a crewed-spaceflight vehicle or a low-Earth-orbit payload.
Incorrect — the target was a geosynchronous transfer orbit, not a lunar trajectory.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: ISRO GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission update; PIB factsheet, 1 November 2026.

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: Under the revamped Periodic Labour Force Survey design introduced from January 2025, the survey year shifted from the earlier July–June cycle to which period?
options: April–March
January–December
October–September
Calendar-year reporting only for urban areas
explanations: Incorrect — April–March is not the cycle specified in the 2025 PLFS redesign.
Correct — MoSPI states that the survey period shifted to January–December with effect from 2025.
Incorrect — the revised PLFS does not use an October–September survey year.
Incorrect — the January–December shift applies to the survey period; the redesign also expands rural and urban high-frequency indicators.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: MoSPI, Annual Report PLFS 2025, explanatory note on the revamped design.

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: The Indira Mahila Shakti Policy–2025 of Telangana describes a shift in the SHG development model primarily from thrift and bank linkage towards:
options: Replacing SHGs with individual cash transfers
Restricting SHGs to savings meetings
Micro-enterprises, livelihood activity and wealth creation
Making SHGs responsible for municipal taxation
explanations: Incorrect — the policy retains the SHG ecosystem rather than replacing it with individual transfers.
Incorrect — the stated objective goes beyond savings meetings and bank linkage.
Correct — the policy emphasises livelihood initiatives, micro-enterprise development, skills, market access and wealth creation through SHGs.
Incorrect — municipal taxation is not the policy's stated purpose.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Indira Mahila Shakti Policy 2025; SERP Telangana.

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: The principal purpose of Telangana's Rythu Bharosa assistance is to provide farmers with:
options: A one-time crop-export subsidy
Agricultural investment support for crop-cycle requirements
A universal pension unrelated to cultivation
Compensation only after a notified natural disaster
explanations: Incorrect — the scheme is not framed as an export subsidy.
Correct — the State describes Rythu Bharosa as agricultural investment assistance intended to provide working capital around crop cycles.
Incorrect — a universal pension is a different type of social-security instrument.
Incorrect — post-disaster compensation is not the scheme's primary design.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Rythu Bharosa scheme description and 2026 release.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the World Health Organization?
options: It is a specialised agency of the United Nations
It is a principal organ of the United Nations with veto-wielding members
It is a regional development bank
It is a treaty court for trade disputes
explanations: Correct — WHO is the UN specialised agency concerned with international public health.
Incorrect — the principal UN organs include the Security Council; WHO is not one of them.
Incorrect — WHO does not function as a development bank.
Incorrect — trade disputes are handled through WTO mechanisms, not WHO.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations and Events; source/basis: United Nations system and WHO Constitution; WHO official institutional profile.

questions.stem: A Party to the Paris Agreement communicates a nationally determined contribution (NDC). Which statement best captures the NDC mechanism?
options: Every country must adopt an identical emissions-reduction percentage
An NDC is prepared only once and cannot be updated
Parties prepare and communicate successive NDCs and pursue domestic mitigation measures
NDCs are binding allocations issued by the UNFCCC Secretariat
explanations: Incorrect — the Paris Agreement recognises nationally determined contributions rather than one identical target for all countries.
Incorrect — parties are expected to communicate successive NDCs, not a one-time unchangeable document.
Correct — Article 4 requires parties to prepare, communicate and maintain successive NDCs and pursue domestic mitigation measures.
Incorrect — the Secretariat does not assign each country's NDC as a centrally imposed quota.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations and Events; source/basis: UNFCCC, Paris Agreement, Article 4.

questions.stem: At the 2023 New Delhi G20 Summit, which organisation was admitted as a permanent member of the G20?
options: ASEAN
African Union
European Free Trade Association
Commonwealth Secretariat
explanations: Incorrect — ASEAN was not the organisation admitted as a new permanent G20 member at the summit.
Correct — the African Union was admitted as a permanent G20 member at the New Delhi Summit.
Incorrect — EFTA was not admitted as a permanent G20 member.
Incorrect — the Commonwealth Secretariat was not the organisation admitted.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations and Events; source/basis: G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration, September 2023.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.stem: A silicon crystal is doped with a trivalent acceptor impurity such as boron. Which carrier becomes the majority carrier?
options: Electrons
Protons
Holes
Neutrons
explanations: Incorrect — electrons are majority carriers in n-type material formed by donor doping.
Incorrect — protons are not mobile majority charge carriers in doped silicon.
Correct — an acceptor impurity produces holes as the majority carriers in p-type silicon.
Incorrect — neutrons are electrically neutral and do not carry semiconductor current.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology; source/basis: Standard semiconductor physics; NCERT Physics, semiconductor electronics.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.stem: An mRNA vaccine works mainly by delivering:
options: Genetic instructions that let host cells produce a target antigen
A live disease-causing pathogen that replicates without control
A complete antibody repertoire harvested from another person
A permanent replacement for the recipient's chromosomes
explanations: Correct — the mRNA is translated by host-cell machinery to produce an antigen that stimulates an immune response.
Incorrect — an mRNA vaccine does not contain a replicating live pathogen.
Incorrect — the vaccine supplies instructions for antigen production, not ready-made antibodies.
Incorrect — mRNA does not permanently replace chromosomes.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology; source/basis: WHO, mRNA vaccine technology explainer; standard molecular biology.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.stem: During discharge of a conventional lithium-ion cell, which description is correct?
options: Electrons pass through the electrolyte while lithium ions pass through the external wire
Lithium ions move from cathode to anode through the separator
No ionic movement occurs; only electrons move
Lithium ions move from anode to cathode through the electrolyte while electrons travel through the external circuit
explanations: Incorrect — electrons travel through the external circuit; the electrolyte carries ions, not electrons.
Incorrect — during discharge, lithium ions move from anode towards cathode.
Incorrect — ionic movement through the electrolyte is essential to maintain charge balance.
Correct — Li⁺ ions migrate through the electrolyte/separator from anode to cathode while electrons flow through the external load.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology; source/basis: Standard electrochemistry; U.S. Department of Energy battery fundamentals.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction covers which period?
explanations: Incorrect — 2005–2015 corresponds to the Hyogo Framework period.
Correct — the Sendai Framework was adopted for 2015–2030.
Incorrect — 2020–2040 is not the adopted Sendai period.
Incorrect — 2030–2050 is not the Sendai Framework period.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies; source/basis: UNDRR, Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: A lake receives excessive nitrate- and phosphate-rich runoff. Which sequence is most characteristic of eutrophication?
options: Nutrient enrichment, algal bloom, decomposition and reduced dissolved oxygen
Nutrient depletion, reduced algae and permanent oxygen increase
Salinity reduction followed by glacier formation
Thermal inversion followed by ozone-layer recovery
explanations: Correct — excess nutrients trigger algal growth; decomposition raises oxygen demand and may cause hypoxia.
Incorrect — eutrophication begins with nutrient enrichment and often reduces dissolved oxygen.
Incorrect — salinity and glacier formation are not the defining causal sequence.
Incorrect — atmospheric inversion and ozone recovery are unrelated to lake nutrient loading.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies; source/basis: UNEP freshwater eutrophication materials; standard environmental science.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: Which combination most directly contributes to the urban heat-island effect?
options: Higher tree cover and greater evaporative cooling
Lower building density and more permeable soil
Heat-storing built surfaces, reduced vegetation and anthropogenic waste heat
Increased albedo in all urban surfaces and no energy use
explanations: Incorrect — vegetation and evapotranspiration generally cool urban environments.
Incorrect — lower density and permeable green surfaces tend to reduce heat storage.
Correct — asphalt and concrete store heat, vegetation is reduced, and vehicles/buildings release waste heat.
Incorrect — higher reflectivity can mitigate heat; urban energy use also produces waste heat.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies; source/basis: UNEP, urban heat-island and urban nature guidance.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.stem: Demand-pull inflation is most likely when:
options: Aggregate demand rises faster than the economy's productive capacity
Production costs fall while demand remains unchanged
The general price level falls continuously
The currency appreciates while import prices decline
explanations: Correct — demand-pull pressure occurs when aggregate demand grows beyond the economy's ability to supply at existing prices.
Incorrect — falling costs tend to reduce, not create, cost pressure.
Incorrect — a continuously falling price level is deflation, not inflation.
Incorrect — currency appreciation and lower import prices can reduce imported inflation.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana; source/basis: Standard macroeconomics; NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.stem: A tax is progressive when:
options: The average tax rate rises as income rises
Every taxpayer pays the same absolute amount
The marginal tax rate remains constant at every income level
Tax is charged only on imported goods
explanations: Correct — progressivity means the average tax burden rises as income or the tax base increases.
Incorrect — an equal absolute payment is a lump-sum structure, not progressive taxation.
Incorrect — a constant marginal rate is characteristic of a proportional-rate structure, not a progressive schedule.
Incorrect — an import tariff is not the defining feature of progressivity.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana; source/basis: UNDP, Human Development Report technical notes.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.stem: A tax schedule is progressive when:
options: Every taxpayer pays the same absolute amount
The average tax rate necessarily falls as income rises
The marginal tax rate rises as the tax base or income rises
Tax is charged only on imported goods
explanations: Incorrect — an equal absolute payment is a lump-sum structure, not progressive taxation.
Incorrect — a falling average rate is associated with a regressive pattern, not progressive taxation.
Correct — under a progressive structure, higher portions of the tax base face higher marginal rates.
Incorrect — an import tariff is not the defining feature of progressivity.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana; source/basis: Standard public economics; Government of India tax-policy terminology.

questions.topic: Physical, Social and Economic Geography of India
questions.stem: Western Disturbances are especially important for which Indian weather pattern?
options: Summer monsoon rainfall along the Tamil Nadu coast
Winter precipitation over north-western India
Cyclonic rainfall confined to the Andaman Sea
Pre-monsoon thunderstorms only in the northeast
explanations: Incorrect — Tamil Nadu's principal northeast-monsoon rainfall is not caused by Western Disturbances.
Correct — these eastward-moving extra-tropical systems bring winter rain to north-western India and snowfall to the western Himalaya.
Incorrect — they are not cyclones confined to the Andaman Sea.
Incorrect — they are not limited to pre-monsoon thunderstorms in the northeast.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Physical, Social and Economic Geography of India; source/basis: India Meteorological Department, Western Disturbances and winter precipitation guidance.

questions.topic: Physical, Social and Economic Geography of India
questions.stem: Laterite soils commonly develop in regions with high temperature and heavy rainfall because these conditions promote:
options: Accumulation of soluble salts without leaching
Glacial deposition of fine sediments
Intense chemical weathering and leaching of silica and bases
Deposition of wind-blown loess
explanations: Incorrect — strong rainfall generally promotes leaching rather than salt accumulation.
Incorrect — glacial deposition is not the process responsible for laterite formation in tropical settings.
Correct — intense weathering and leaching remove silica and bases, leaving iron- and aluminium-rich material.
Incorrect — loess is wind-deposited silt, not laterite.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Physical, Social and Economic Geography of India; source/basis: NCERT, India: Physical Environment, soils; standard geomorphology.

questions.topic: Physical, Social and Economic Geography and Demography of Telangana
questions.stem: Most of Telangana lies within which broad physiographic region of India?
options: The Indo-Gangetic Plain
The Deccan Plateau
The Eastern Coastal Plain
The Himalayan foothills
explanations: Incorrect — Telangana is south of the Indo-Gangetic alluvial plain.
Correct — Telangana is predominantly part of the peninsular Deccan Plateau.
Incorrect — the Eastern Coastal Plain lies farther east along the coast.
Incorrect — Telangana is not part of the Himalayan foothills.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Physical, Social and Economic Geography and Demography of Telangana; source/basis: Government of Telangana, state geography overview; NCERT, India: Physical Environment.

questions.topic: Physical, Social and Economic Geography and Demography of Telangana
questions.stem: The parent material most closely associated with the formation of extensive black cotton soils of the Deccan region is:
options: Basaltic lava flows
Recent coral reefs
Glacial till
Wind-deposited desert sand
explanations: Correct — much of the Deccan black-soil region is associated with weathering of basaltic lava flows.
Incorrect — coral reefs are not the parent material of Deccan regur soils.
Incorrect — glacial till is not the source of these tropical Deccan soils.
Incorrect — desert sand forms sandy soils, not characteristic shrink-swell black soils.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Physical, Social and Economic Geography and Demography of Telangana; source/basis: NCERT, India: Physical Environment, Deccan Trap and black soils.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Modern India with special emphasis on Indian National Movement
questions.stem: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is historically significant because it:
options: Was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League on constitutional demands
Ended the Non-Cooperation Movement
Created the Indian National Army
Announced the partition of Bengal
explanations: Correct — the 1916 pact marked cooperation between Congress and the Muslim League on constitutional reforms and representation.
Incorrect — the Non-Cooperation Movement began later, in 1920.
Incorrect — the Indian National Army was formed in a later period.
Incorrect — the partition of Bengal occurred in 1905 and was annulled in 1911.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Modern India with special emphasis on Indian National Movement; source/basis: NCERT, Indian National Movement; Lucknow Pact, 1916.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Modern India with special emphasis on Indian National Movement
questions.stem: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 primarily concerned the grievances of:
options: Textile mill owners over import duties
Indigo cultivators subjected to oppressive plantation arrangements
Railway workers over working hours
Forest communities opposing the Forest Acts
explanations: Incorrect — the movement was not a dispute led by textile mill owners.
Correct — Gandhi's Champaran intervention addressed indigo cultivators and coercive plantation practices.
Incorrect — railway labour disputes were not the central issue at Champaran.
Incorrect — Champaran focused on indigo cultivation, not forest rights.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Modern India with special emphasis on Indian National Movement; source/basis: NCERT, Indian National Movement; Gandhi's Champaran campaign.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state
questions.stem: In the former Hyderabad State, the Mulki rules were primarily associated with:
options: Domicile-based conditions for eligibility to specified public employment
Regulation of inter-state river-water sharing
A tax on imported textiles
Election of members to the Constituent Assembly
explanations: Correct — Mulki rules concerned local-status or domicile conditions for eligibility in public services in the former Hyderabad State.
Incorrect — river-water sharing is a separate administrative and constitutional subject.
Incorrect — the rules were not a customs or textile-tax measure.
Incorrect — they did not govern election to the Constituent Assembly.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state; source/basis: Standard Telangana history; Hyderabad State service rules and Telangana movement history.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state
questions.stem: The Sri Krishna Committee appointed in 2010 was asked by the Union Government primarily to:
options: Recommend a new national language
Examine the situation in Andhra Pradesh with reference to the demand for a separate Telangana
Redraw the boundaries of all southern States
Prepare the first Telangana State budget
explanations: Incorrect — language policy was not the committee's mandate.
Correct — the committee examined the situation in Andhra Pradesh in the context of the demand for separate Telangana.
Incorrect — its remit was not a nationwide boundary reorganisation exercise.
Incorrect — Telangana had not yet become a separate State when the committee was appointed.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state; source/basis: Ministry of Home Affairs, Terms of Reference and report of the Committee for Consultations on the Situation in Andhra Pradesh (2010–11).

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: A person seeks enforcement of a Fundamental Right directly from the Supreme Court. Which constitutional provision expressly guarantees the right to move that Court for this purpose?
options: Article 19
Article 32
Article 110
Article 280
explanations: Incorrect — Article 19 lists specified freedoms; it is not the express remedy provision asked for.
Correct — Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Incorrect — Article 110 defines a Money Bill.
Incorrect — Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; source/basis: Constitution of India, Article 32; Legislative Department edition 2025.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
options: Article 148
Article 124
Article 324
Article 356
explanations: Correct — Article 148 establishes the office of the CAG and provides for appointment and related safeguards.
Incorrect — Article 124 concerns the Supreme Court.
Incorrect — Article 324 concerns the Election Commission's powers.
Incorrect — Article 356 concerns failure of constitutional machinery in a State.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; source/basis: Constitution of India, Article 148; Legislative Department edition 2025.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: Under Article 123, when may the President promulgate an ordinance?
options: Only when both Houses of Parliament are in session
When at least one House of Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that immediate action is necessary
Only after authorisation by the Supreme Court
Whenever a State Legislature is not in session
explanations: Incorrect — Article 123 permits an ordinance in the situation where Parliament is not fully in session, not when both Houses are sitting.
Correct — the constitutional condition is that, except when both Houses are in session, the President may act if satisfied that circumstances require immediate action.
Incorrect — prior Supreme Court authorisation is not a condition in Article 123.
Incorrect — a State Legislature's session status relates to the Governor's ordinance power under Article 213, not the President's power under Article 123.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; source/basis: Constitution of India, Article 123; Legislative Department edition 2025.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: Article 200 of the Constitution deals with the Governor's action when:
options: A Money Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha
A constitutional amendment is passed by Parliament
A State Legislature's Bill is presented to the Governor for assent
A Supreme Court judgment is delivered
explanations: Incorrect — introduction of a Money Bill in the Lok Sabha is governed by other constitutional provisions.
Incorrect — Article 200 concerns State Bills presented to the Governor, not parliamentary constitutional amendments.
Correct — Article 200 sets out the Governor's options on a Bill passed by the State Legislature and presented for assent.
Incorrect — Article 200 is not a provision governing Supreme Court judgments.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; source/basis: Constitution of India, Article 200; Legislative Department edition 2025.

questions.topic: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies
questions.stem: Which practice is expressly abolished by Article 17 of the Constitution?
options: Untouchability
Titles of academic degrees
All forms of private property
All religious institutions
explanations: Correct — Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
Incorrect — academic degrees are not the practice addressed by Article 17.
Incorrect — Article 17 does not abolish private property.
Incorrect — Article 17 does not abolish religious institutions.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies; source/basis: Constitution of India, Article 17; Legislative Department edition 2025.

questions.topic: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies
questions.stem: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, the term 'person with benchmark disability' generally refers to a person with not less than what percentage of a specified disability, as certified?
explanations: Incorrect — 20% is below the statutory benchmark threshold.
Correct — section 2(r) uses a threshold of not less than 40% for the specified disability where it is not defined in measurable terms, subject to certification.
Incorrect — 60% is not the statutory minimum benchmark threshold.
Incorrect — 80% is not the statutory minimum benchmark threshold.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies; source/basis: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, section 2(r); India Code.

questions.topic: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies
questions.stem: Article 15(3) permits the State to make special provisions for:
options: Only government employees
Only linguistic minorities
Women and children
Only persons holding constitutional office
explanations: Incorrect — Article 15(3) is not restricted to government employees.
Incorrect — linguistic-minority safeguards arise under other constitutional provisions.
Correct — Article 15(3) expressly permits special provisions for women and children.
Incorrect — constitutional office-holders are not the class specified in Article 15(3).
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies; source/basis: Constitution of India, Article 15(3); Legislative Department edition 2025.

questions.topic: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana
questions.stem: Oggu Katha is best described as a Telangana folk tradition involving:
options: A classical instrumental ensemble without narration
A martial horse-riding contest
Musical storytelling, often narrating legends associated with Mallanna
A textile tie-dye process
explanations: Incorrect — Oggu Katha is a narrative performance tradition, not merely an instrumental ensemble.
Incorrect — it is not a horse-riding contest.
Correct — Oggu Katha is a folk storytelling form using music and narration, including stories associated with Mallanna.
Incorrect — textile tie-dyeing is associated with Ikat traditions, not Oggu Katha.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Language and Culture / district culture pages.

questions.topic: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana
questions.stem: What is characteristic of the yarn-dyeing process used in Pochampally Ikat?
options: Yarns are resist-dyed in planned patterns before weaving
The finished cloth is painted only after weaving
The design is produced solely by metallic embroidery
The pattern is created by printing a photograph onto the fabric
explanations: Correct — Ikat patterns are created by resist-dyeing selected yarn sections before the yarn is woven.
Incorrect — post-weaving painting is not the defining Ikat method.
Incorrect — metallic embroidery is a different textile embellishment technique.
Incorrect — photographic printing is unrelated to traditional Ikat weaving.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; source/basis: Telangana Tourism, heritage and handicrafts overview; standard textile-process description.

questions.topic: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana
questions.stem: Gussadi is a traditional dance form associated particularly with which tribal community of Telangana?
options: Gond community
Toda community
Bhil community of western India only
Lepcha community
explanations: Correct — Gussadi is associated with the Gond community, particularly in the Adilabad region of Telangana.
Incorrect — the Toda community is associated with the Nilgiri region.
Incorrect — Gussadi is not a dance tradition of the Bhil community alone.
Incorrect — the Lepcha community is associated with the eastern Himalaya.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; source/basis: Telangana Tourism, heritage experience and folk traditions.

questions.stem: The Telangana Gruha Jyothi scheme is described by the State as providing eligible households with free electricity up to:
options: 50 units per month
100 units per month
150 units per month
200 units per month
explanations: Incorrect — 50 units is below the scheme's stated monthly ceiling.
Incorrect — 100 units is not the published ceiling.
Incorrect — 150 units is not the published ceiling.
Correct — the official State scheme description states free electricity up to 200 units per month for eligible households.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Policies of Telangana State; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Government Initiatives / Gruha Jyothi scheme page.

questions.stem: The Telangana Cheyutha initiative, implemented through the Rajiv Arogyasri framework, is described on the State portal as providing health coverage of up to:
options: ₹1 lakh per family
₹2 lakh per family
₹10 lakh per family
₹25 lakh per individual
explanations: Incorrect — ₹1 lakh is below the coverage stated on the State portal.
Incorrect — ₹2 lakh is not the stated scheme ceiling.
Correct — the Telangana State portal describes Cheyutha as providing health coverage up to ₹10 lakh per family under the Rajiv Arogyasri initiative.
Incorrect — ₹25 lakh per individual is not the scheme amount described by the State portal.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Policies of Telangana State; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Government Initiatives, Cheyutha scheme.

questions.stem: Which policy instrument best describes Rythu Bharosa as presented by the Telangana Agriculture Department?
options: Seasonal agricultural investment assistance to eligible cultivators
A crop-export tariff imposed on farmers
A universal old-age pension
A subsidy paid only to fertiliser manufacturers
explanations: Correct — the scheme is framed as agricultural investment support for farmers around crop cycles.
Incorrect — it is not an export tariff.
Incorrect — an old-age pension is a social-security programme of a different type.
Incorrect — the assistance is not restricted to fertiliser manufacturers.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Policies of Telangana State; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Agriculture and Cooperation Department; Rythu Bharosa.

questions.topic: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation
questions.stem: Statements: All water meters are devices. No device is an animal. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: Some water meters are animals
No water meter is an animal
All animals are water meters
Some devices are not water meters
explanations: Incorrect — this contradicts the statement that no device is an animal.
Correct — every water meter is a device, and no device is an animal; therefore no water meter is an animal.
Incorrect — the premises do not state that animals are water meters.
Incorrect — the premises do not establish that any device exists outside the class of water meters.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation; source/basis: Logical Reasoning; standard categorical-syllogism rules.

questions.topic: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation
questions.stem: Four municipal zones report treated-water output of 120, 150, 90 and 140 million litres per day. What percentage of the combined output is contributed by the zone producing 150 million litres per day?
explanations: Incorrect — 20% would correspond to 100 of the 500 million litres.
Incorrect — 25% would correspond to 125 million litres.
Incorrect — 35% would correspond to 175 million litres.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation; source/basis: Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation; calculation from stated data.

questions.stem: Choose the grammatically correct completion: 'Neither the chief engineer nor the technicians ___ available during the inspection.'
options: is
has been
was
were
explanations: Incorrect — with neither…nor, the verb normally agrees with the nearer subject; 'technicians' is plural.
Incorrect — 'has been' is singular and does not agree with the nearer plural subject.
Incorrect — 'was' is singular and does not agree with 'technicians'.
Correct — the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'technicians', so the plural form 'were' is used.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Basic English (10th class Standard); source/basis: Basic English; standard subject–verb agreement rules.

questions.stem: A component independently fails a quality check with probability 0.2. In a sample of five components, what is the probability that exactly two fail?
explanations: Incorrect — this does not apply the binomial coefficient and the stated failure/success probabilities.
Incorrect — 0.4096 is not the probability for exactly two failures under the stated parameters.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; source/basis: OpenStax, Introductory Statistics, binomial distribution.

questions.stem: A Poisson process has an average of two events per interval. What is the probability of observing zero events in one such interval?
explanations: Correct — for λ=2, P(X=0)=e⁻²(2⁰/0!)=e⁻².
Incorrect — e⁻¹ corresponds to λ=1, not the stated mean.
Incorrect — 2e⁻² is the probability of exactly one event when λ=2.
Incorrect — 1−e⁻² is the probability of at least one event.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; source/basis: OpenStax, Introductory Statistics, Poisson distribution.

questions.stem: A random variable X has variance 5. What is Var(3X−4)?
explanations: Incorrect — multiplication by 3 changes variance by the square of 3.
Incorrect — variance is not multiplied by the absolute scale factor alone.
Incorrect — adding or subtracting a constant does not add 4 to variance.
Correct — Var(aX+b)=a²Var(X), so Var(3X−4)=9×5=45.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; source/basis: Standard probability and statistics; linear transformation of variance.

questions.stem: For the upper-triangular matrix [[2, 5], [0, 3]], what are its eigenvalues?
options: 5 and 0
2 and 3
−2 and −3
1 and 6
explanations: Incorrect — 5 is an off-diagonal entry and is not an eigenvalue here.
Correct — the characteristic polynomial of a triangular matrix is determined by its diagonal entries, so its eigenvalues are 2 and 3.
Incorrect — the diagonal entries are positive and the eigenvalues are not their negatives.
Incorrect — the sum and product are 5 and 6, but the eigenvalues themselves are 2 and 3.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Standard linear algebra; eigenvalues of triangular matrices.

questions.stem: On the integers, define a relation aRb when 4 divides (a−b). Which set is the equivalence class of 1?
options: All integers divisible by 4
All odd integers
explanations: Incorrect — integers divisible by 4 form the equivalence class of 0.
Incorrect — odd integers congruent to 3 modulo 4 are excluded.
Correct — the class contains exactly integers of the form 1+4k for integer k.
Incorrect — this omits negative representatives and includes numbers not congruent to 1 modulo 4.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications; equivalence relations.

questions.stem: If A and B are square matrices of the same order with det(A)=3 and det(B)=−2, what is det(AB)?
explanations: Correct — det(AB)=det(A)det(B)=3×(−2)=−6.
Incorrect — −1 is not the product of the given determinants.
Incorrect — the product is negative six, not one.
Incorrect — the sign is negative because det(B) is negative.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Standard linear algebra; multiplicative property of determinants.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: A finite undirected graph is connected and has at least one edge. Which condition is necessary and sufficient for it to contain an Euler circuit?
options: Exactly two vertices have odd degree
Every vertex has even degree
Every vertex has degree two
The graph must be a tree
explanations: Incorrect — exactly two odd-degree vertices characterise an open Euler trail, not an Euler circuit.
Correct — a connected undirected graph has an Euler circuit exactly when every vertex has even degree.
Incorrect — degree two at every vertex is sufficient for a connected cycle but is not necessary for all Eulerian graphs.
Incorrect — a tree is not generally Eulerian.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic; source/basis: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications; Euler's theorem.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: In a class of 100 candidates, 40 study database systems, 35 study networks and 15 study both. How many study at least one of the two subjects?
explanations: Incorrect — 45 undercounts the union by subtracting too much overlap.
Incorrect — 50 does not apply the stated overlap correctly.
Incorrect — 75 is the sum without subtracting the intersection.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic; source/basis: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications; inclusion–exclusion principle.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: Let T(0)=0 and T(n)=2T(n−1)+1 for n≥1. What is the closed form of T(n)?
options: n²
2ⁿ
explanations: Incorrect — 2n+1 grows linearly and fails the recurrence for n≥2.
Correct — solving the recurrence gives T(n)=2ⁿ−1; substitution verifies 2(2ⁿ⁻¹−1)+1=2ⁿ−1.
Incorrect — n² does not satisfy the recurrence.
Incorrect — 2ⁿ is one larger than the required solution for T(0)=0.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic; source/basis: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications; recurrence relations.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: Thirteen people are assigned birthdays by month only. What must be true?
options: At least one month contains birthdays of two or more people
Every month contains at least one birthday
Exactly one month contains two birthdays
At least two months are empty
explanations: Correct — placing 13 people into 12 month categories forces at least one category to contain two or more people.
Incorrect — the people need not be distributed across all 12 months.
Incorrect — the principle guarantees a collision, not exactly one month with two people.
Incorrect — the distribution could include no empty month if some months have multiple people.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic; source/basis: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications; pigeonhole principle.

questions.stem: A four-bit odd-parity generator must output 1 exactly when the four data bits contain an odd number of 1s. Which gate operation combines the four bits to produce that parity bit?
options: AND of all four bits
OR of all four bits
XOR of all four bits
XNOR of all four bits
explanations: Incorrect — AND is 1 only when all four bits are 1, not whenever their count is odd.
Incorrect — OR is 1 for any nonzero input and does not distinguish odd from even parity.
Correct — cascading XOR gates produce 1 for an odd number of input 1s and 0 for an even number.
Incorrect — XNOR gives the complement of the odd-parity XOR result.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; source/basis: M. Morris Mano, Digital Design; parity generation and XOR logic.

questions.stem: For a positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop, what value is transferred to Q at the active clock edge?
options: The complement of D
The value of D immediately before the active edge
The XOR of D and the previous Q
The value of the clock signal
explanations: Incorrect — complementing D describes neither the normal D flip-flop characteristic nor its next-state rule.
Correct — at the active edge, the flip-flop samples D and stores that value as its next Q state.
Incorrect — the D flip-flop does not combine D and the previous Q using XOR.
Incorrect — the clock controls when sampling occurs; it is not the data input.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; source/basis: M. Morris Mano, Digital Design; edge-triggered D flip-flops.

questions.stem: What is the 4-bit Gray-code equivalent of the binary number 1011?
explanations: Incorrect — binary and Gray representations are not identical except for special patterns.
Incorrect — XORing adjacent binary bits does not produce 1101 for 1011.
Correct — keep the most significant bit, then XOR adjacent binary bits to obtain 1110.
Incorrect — 1001 results from an incorrect adjacent-bit conversion.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; source/basis: Standard digital logic; binary and Gray-code conversion.

questions.stem: An ideal pipeline has six stages and executes five instructions with no stalls. How many clock cycles are required from the first instruction entering the pipeline until the fifth instruction completes?
explanations: Incorrect — five cycles would not allow the six-stage latency to be completed.
Incorrect — six cycles completes only the first instruction, not all five.
Correct — an ideal k-stage pipeline needs k+n−1 cycles: 6+5−1=10.
Incorrect — 30 cycles is the non-pipelined total if each of five instructions takes six serial stage cycles.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design; instruction pipelining.

questions.stem: During a block transfer using DMA, which statement is most accurate?
options: The CPU executes a separate load/store instruction for every transferred byte
The DMA controller transfers data between an I/O device and memory, typically interrupting the CPU on completion
The cache controller performs all disk scheduling
The I/O device writes directly into CPU registers without a bus
explanations: Incorrect — DMA avoids CPU handling of every byte or word in the block.
Correct — the DMA controller manages the block transfer over the system bus and can notify the CPU when it finishes.
Incorrect — cache control and disk scheduling are separate functions.
Incorrect — DMA transfers involve memory and I/O interfaces, not direct writing into CPU registers.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design; DMA and I/O interfaces.

questions.stem: In low-order memory interleaving across multiple equal-sized banks, how are consecutive memory addresses typically distributed?
options: Consecutive addresses are placed in successive banks in round-robin order
All consecutive addresses are placed in bank zero
Every address is replicated in every bank
Addresses are assigned only by the CPU opcode
explanations: Correct — low-order interleaving uses low-order address bits to select banks, distributing consecutive words among successive banks.
Incorrect — placing all consecutive addresses in one bank would not provide interleaving.
Incorrect — interleaving distributes addresses; it does not replicate every word.
Incorrect — memory-bank selection is based on address bits, not the instruction opcode.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design; memory interleaving.

questions.stem: In C, a function receives an ordinary integer parameter by value. If the function assigns a new value to that parameter, what happens to the caller's original integer variable?
options: It is necessarily changed
It is unchanged unless the function receives and uses its address through a pointer
It becomes a global variable
The program has undefined behaviour
explanations: Incorrect — ordinary scalar arguments are copied into the function parameter; assignment does not directly modify the caller's object.
Correct — passing a pointer to the caller's object and dereferencing it is the usual way to modify that object from the function.
Incorrect — parameter passing does not change an object's storage duration or scope to global.
Incorrect — assigning to a by-value parameter is well-defined and does not itself cause undefined behaviour.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: ISO C standard N1570; function-call argument semantics.

questions.stem: In a max-heap represented as a binary tree, which ordering condition must hold for every parent with children?
options: The parent key is no greater than either child key
The parent key is at least as large as each child key
Every node has exactly two children
The left subtree must contain only even keys
explanations: Incorrect — that is the min-heap ordering condition.
Correct — a max-heap requires each parent key to be greater than or equal to its children.
Incorrect — a binary heap is complete but need not be a full binary tree.
Incorrect — heap order has no parity restriction on keys.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: OpenDSA, Binary Heaps; standard data-structures texts.

questions.stem: For a binary search tree whose keys are distinct, which traversal outputs the keys in ascending order?
options: Preorder
Postorder
Inorder
Level order
explanations: Incorrect — preorder visits root before subtrees and is not generally sorted.
Incorrect — postorder visits children before root and is not generally sorted.
Correct — inorder traversal visits left subtree, node, then right subtree; the BST ordering property makes the output ascending.
Incorrect — level order visits nodes by depth and does not preserve sorted key order.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: OpenDSA, Binary Search Trees; inorder traversal.

questions.stem: A recursive factorial routine makes one call for each integer from n down to 1 and uses constant local storage per call. What is its auxiliary call-stack space complexity?
options: O(log n)
O(n)
O(n log n)
explanations: Incorrect — constant local storage per call does not make the total stack constant when calls accumulate.
Incorrect — the recursion depth decreases by one per call, not by halving n.
Correct — there are Θ(n) simultaneously active calls in the usual recursive implementation, each using O(1) local storage.
Incorrect — no logarithmic factor is introduced by this linear-depth recursion.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: Standard data-structures texts; recursion depth and auxiliary stack space.

questions.stem: A topological ordering of all vertices of a directed graph exists if and only if the graph is:
options: A complete graph
A directed acyclic graph
An undirected tree
A graph in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree
explanations: Incorrect — a complete directed graph with cycles need not have a topological ordering.
Correct — topological ordering is defined for a directed acyclic graph; a directed cycle makes the required ordering impossible.
Incorrect — an undirected tree is not the directed-graph condition for topological ordering.
Incorrect — equal in-degree and out-degree does not imply acyclicity.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms; topological sorting of DAGs.

questions.stem: For a graph represented by a V×V distance matrix, what is the time complexity of the Floyd–Warshall all-pairs shortest-path algorithm?
options: O(V)
O(V²)
O(V³)
O(V⁴)
explanations: Incorrect — the algorithm examines combinations of source, destination and intermediate vertices.
Incorrect — V² is the matrix size, not the full triple-loop running time.
Correct — three nested loops over vertices give O(V³) time.
Incorrect — there are three, not four, vertex-index loops in the standard algorithm.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms; all-pairs shortest paths.

questions.stem: A dynamic array doubles its capacity whenever it becomes full. Over a sequence of n append operations, what is the amortized time per append?
options: Θ(log n)
Θ(n)
Θ(n log n)
explanations: Incorrect — logarithmic resizing events occur, but their total copying cost is linear across n appends.
Correct — geometric growth makes the total number of copied elements O(n), so the amortized append cost is Θ(1).
Incorrect — an individual resize can cost Θ(n), but that is not the amortized cost per append.
Incorrect — the aggregate copying cost does not grow as n log n under doubling.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms; amortized analysis of dynamic tables.

questions.stem: In the dynamic-programming recurrence for the longest common subsequence of strings X and Y, what is L[i,j] when X[i] equals Y[j]?
options: max(L[i−1,j],L[i,j−1])+1 regardless of symbols
explanations: Incorrect — adding the two neighbouring values is not the recurrence for a matching final character.
Correct — when the current characters match, the LCS length is one plus the LCS of the two preceding prefixes.
Incorrect — the maximum-of-neighbours recurrence applies when the characters differ, without the extra 1.
Incorrect — a matching character extends the previous common subsequence rather than resetting it to zero.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms; dynamic programming and longest common subsequence.

questions.stem: Which language over {a,b} is a standard example of a language recognised by a pushdown automaton but not by a finite automaton?
options: {aⁿbⁿ | n≥0}
The set of all strings ending in a
The set of strings containing at least one b
explanations: Incorrect — {a,b}* is regular and can be recognised by a finite automaton.
Correct — a PDA can push for each a and pop for each matching b, while a finite automaton cannot remember an unbounded count.
Incorrect — strings ending in a form a regular language.
Incorrect — strings containing at least one b form a regular language.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation; context-free languages and PDAs.

questions.stem: If L is a regular language over alphabet Σ, which language is guaranteed to be regular?
options: The complement Σ*\L
Only the finite subsets of L
The set of all non-halting Turing-machine inputs
The set of all context-free languages
explanations: Correct — regular languages are closed under complement; a complete DFA can be complemented by swapping accepting and non-accepting states.
Incorrect — regular languages need not be finite, and this is not a closure operation.
Incorrect — non-halting inputs for arbitrary Turing machines need not form a regular language.
Incorrect — a class of languages is not the complement operation on L.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation; closure properties.

questions.stem: A Turing machine decides a language L if it:
options: Accepts every string and never rejects
May loop forever on strings not in L
Halts on every input, accepting strings in L and rejecting strings not in L
Uses only a finite number of tape cells on every input
explanations: Incorrect — a decider must reject strings outside L as well as accept strings inside L.
Incorrect — looping forever is permitted for a recogniser on some non-members, but not for a decider.
Correct — decidability requires a machine that halts on every input with the correct yes/no answer.
Incorrect — a decider may use unbounded tape as a function of input length; finite-space restriction is not the definition.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation; decidability.

questions.stem: During construction of an LL(1) predictive parsing table, two different productions for the same nonterminal are placed in the same table cell. What does this indicate?
options: The grammar is necessarily LL(1)
The grammar has a parsing-table conflict and is not LL(1) under that table construction
The grammar is regular
The grammar contains no nullable productions
explanations: Incorrect — an LL(1) table must select at most one production for a nonterminal/lookahead pair.
Correct — a multiple-entry cell creates a predictive parsing conflict, so the grammar is not LL(1) as written.
Incorrect — an LL(1) conflict does not imply the grammar is regular.
Incorrect — conflicts can arise with or without nullable productions.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; source/basis: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers; predictive parsing and LL(1) tables.

questions.stem: Why can a directly left-recursive production such as E → E + T cause a naive recursive-descent parser to fail?
options: It makes every token appear as an identifier
It prevents the grammar from generating any finite string
The parser may call the same procedure recursively without consuming input
It forces the parser to use a symbol table before scanning
explanations: Incorrect — left recursion does not change the lexical class of tokens.
Incorrect — left-recursive context-free grammars can generate finite strings.
Correct — a top-down procedure may re-enter E before consuming any input, causing unbounded recursion.
Incorrect — symbol-table construction order is not the cause of this parsing problem.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; source/basis: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers; grammar transformations and top-down parsing.

questions.stem: For the expression x = a + b * c, which three-address-code sequence preserves the usual multiplication-before-addition precedence?
options: t1 = a + b; t2 = t1 * c; x = t2
t1 = b * c; t2 = a + t1; x = t2
t1 = a * c; t2 = b + t1; x = t2
x = a + b; t1 = t1 * c
explanations: Incorrect — this sequence adds a and b before multiplying, changing the expression's meaning.
Correct — it computes b*c first, adds a, and assigns the result to x.
Incorrect — it multiplies a and c, which is not the stated expression.
Incorrect — the sequence is incomplete and changes the intended grouping.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; source/basis: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers; intermediate-code generation.

questions.stem: A counting semaphore is initialised to 3 and each process must successfully wait on it before entering a protected service. Assuming correct wait/signal use, what is the maximum number of processes simultaneously inside?
options: Unlimited
explanations: Incorrect — a value of 3 permits more than one concurrent entrant when each entrant consumes one permit.
Incorrect — the semaphore has three permits, not two.
Correct — at most three successful waits can consume the three available permits simultaneously.
Incorrect — the semaphore bounds concurrent entry by its count.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts; counting semaphores.

questions.stem: In round-robin CPU scheduling, what tends to happen when the time quantum is made extremely large compared with typical CPU bursts?
options: It approaches FCFS behaviour
It becomes shortest-job-first scheduling
It guarantees zero waiting time
It prevents context switches permanently
explanations: Correct — with a very large quantum, processes usually finish their CPU bursts before pre-emption, so behaviour approaches FCFS.
Incorrect — round-robin does not become SJF merely by increasing its quantum.
Incorrect — a large quantum does not guarantee zero waiting time.
Incorrect — context switches still occur on blocking, completion or other scheduling events.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts; CPU scheduling.

questions.stem: In a traditional Unix-like file system, which statement about an inode is correct?
options: It stores the filename as its only content
It stores file metadata and references to data blocks; directory entries map names to inode numbers
It contains the full contents of every file in the directory
It is a network packet used by TCP
explanations: Incorrect — filenames are stored in directory entries, not as the inode's defining content.
Correct — an inode stores metadata and block-location information, while a directory maps a filename to an inode number.
Incorrect — file data resides in data blocks; the inode does not contain every file's complete contents.
Incorrect — an inode is a file-system data structure, not a TCP packet.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts; file-system implementation.

questions.stem: In indexed file allocation, where are the addresses of a file's data blocks stored?
options: Only in the first data block
In a separate index block associated with the file
In the CPU instruction register
In the directory name string
explanations: Incorrect — the first data block contains file data; it is not necessarily the index structure.
Correct — an index block contains pointers to the file's data blocks, allowing non-contiguous allocation and direct block lookup.
Incorrect — the instruction register is part of CPU control, not file-system allocation metadata.
Incorrect — a directory entry does not store the complete block-address list in its name.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts; file allocation methods.

questions.stem: Let Enrolled(student, course) contain student-course pairs and Required(course) list all compulsory courses. Which relational-algebra operation returns students enrolled in every course listed in Required?
options: Union
Difference
Division
Cartesian product
explanations: Incorrect — union combines tuples from compatible relations; it does not express 'all required courses'.
Incorrect — difference removes tuples and does not test coverage of every required course.
Correct — relational division returns student values paired with all tuples in the divisor relation, matching the 'every required course' condition.
Incorrect — Cartesian product forms all combinations and does not select students who satisfy every required course.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; source/basis: Standard database theory; relational algebra division operator.

questions.stem: Which SQL predicate correctly tests whether column manager_id contains a NULL value?
options: manager_id = NULL
manager_id <> NULL
manager_id IS NULL
NULL(manager_id) = TRUE
explanations: Incorrect — comparisons with NULL using = yield UNKNOWN under SQL three-valued logic.
Incorrect — <> NULL also does not test nullness; the result is UNKNOWN.
Correct — IS NULL is the SQL predicate for testing a null value.
Incorrect — NULL is not used as a scalar function in this expression.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; source/basis: PostgreSQL documentation, comparison predicates; standard SQL NULL semantics.

questions.stem: A precedence graph constructed for a schedule of database transactions contains a directed cycle. What follows?
options: The schedule is conflict-serializable
The schedule is not conflict-serializable
All transactions must have committed
The schedule is necessarily recoverable
explanations: Incorrect — conflict serializability requires an acyclic precedence graph.
Correct — a directed cycle is the standard test showing that the schedule is not conflict-serializable.
Incorrect — the graph's cycle does not determine whether transactions have committed.
Incorrect — recoverability is a separate property and is not established by the cycle test.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; source/basis: Standard database-system texts; conflict-serializability theorem.

questions.stem: Which B+ tree property makes it particularly useful for range queries?
options: All records are stored only in internal nodes
Leaf nodes are typically linked in key order
Every search must visit every leaf
The tree is necessarily unbalanced
explanations: Incorrect — B+ trees store data entries or record pointers at the leaves; internal nodes guide search.
Correct — linked leaf nodes allow sequential traversal across an ordered key range after locating the first key.
Incorrect — a range query can scan only the relevant consecutive leaf entries, not every leaf.
Incorrect — B+ trees are height-balanced.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; source/basis: Standard database-system texts; B+ tree indexes and range retrieval.

questions.stem: In a conventional data-flow modelling approach, a context-level DFD represents the system as:
options: A single process interacting with external entities
Every program statement as a separate process
Only the database tables and indexes
A sequence of CPU instructions
explanations: Correct — the context diagram depicts the whole system as one process and shows its data exchanges with external entities.
Incorrect — statement-level decomposition is far below the context level.
Incorrect — a DFD models data flows and processes, not merely the physical database schema.
Incorrect — CPU instruction sequencing is not the purpose of a context DFD.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: Sommerville, Software Engineering; data-flow modelling.

questions.stem: Which design combination is generally preferred for a maintainable modular software system?
options: Low cohesion and high coupling
High cohesion and low coupling
High cohesion and high coupling
Low cohesion and low cohesion
explanations: Incorrect — unrelated responsibilities and strong interdependence make modules harder to understand and change.
Correct — high cohesion keeps related responsibilities together, while low coupling reduces dependencies between modules.
Incorrect — high cohesion is desirable, but high coupling creates unnecessary inter-module dependence.
Incorrect — the option repeats low cohesion and does not state the preferred design combination.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: Sommerville, Software Engineering; modular design quality.

questions.stem: In the software V-model, acceptance testing is most directly associated with validation of which development artefact?
options: Detailed module design
Source-code formatting rules
User and system requirements
The physical database index layout only
explanations: Incorrect — detailed module design is more directly associated with unit-level verification.
Incorrect — formatting rules are not the development artefact validated by acceptance testing.
Correct — acceptance testing checks whether the delivered system satisfies user and business requirements.
Incorrect — database index layout is too narrow to represent the system requirements being accepted.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: Standard software-engineering texts; V-model and verification/validation mapping.

questions.stem: A developer changes the authentication module. Which test activity is specifically intended to detect unintended effects on previously working features?
options: Regression testing
Load testing only
Acceptance-test planning only
Code generation
explanations: Correct — regression tests rerun relevant existing tests after a change to detect newly introduced failures.
Incorrect — load testing measures performance under workload and may not reveal functional regressions.
Incorrect — planning acceptance tests does not itself detect side effects of the code change.
Incorrect — code generation is a build activity, not a test activity.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: Standard software-engineering texts; regression testing and maintenance.

questions.stem: In cyclic redundancy checking, the sender appends a remainder obtained by:
options: Adding decimal checksums to each byte
Polynomial division over GF(2) using the agreed generator polynomial
Encrypting the frame with the receiver's public key
Counting the number of routers on the path
explanations: Incorrect — CRC is not an ordinary decimal sum of bytes.
Correct — CRC treats bit strings as polynomials over GF(2) and appends the division remainder.
Incorrect — public-key encryption is a different security operation.
Incorrect — router count is unrelated to CRC computation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: Standard data-communications texts; cyclic redundancy check.

questions.stem: OSPF is classified as which type of routing protocol?
options: Distance-vector protocol using hop count only
Link-state protocol that computes shortest paths
Path-vector protocol used only between autonomous systems
Transport-layer reliability protocol
explanations: Incorrect — hop-count distance vector describes RIP more closely, not OSPF.
Correct — OSPF distributes link-state information and computes shortest paths using Dijkstra's algorithm.
Incorrect — path-vector routing is associated with BGP.
Incorrect — OSPF is a network-layer routing protocol, not a transport protocol.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: IETF RFC 2328, OSPF Version 2; routing algorithms.

questions.stem: In a public-key cryptosystem, A wants to send a confidential message to B. Which key should A use to encrypt the message so that B alone can decrypt it?
options: A's private key
A's public key
B's private key
B's public key
explanations: Incorrect — A's private key is not the key used to provide confidentiality to B.
Incorrect — A's public key does not restrict decryption to B.
Incorrect — B's private key must remain secret and is used by B for decryption, not given to A.
Correct — encrypting with B's public key allows the corresponding private key held by B to decrypt the ciphertext.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: NIST cryptographic guidance; public-key encryption and key pairs.

questions.stem: When a DNS resolver receives a recursive query from a client, what responsibility does the resolver accept?
options: Return only the address of the root name server
Return the final answer or an error after performing the necessary lookups
Forward the query unchanged to every authoritative server simultaneously
Convert the domain name into an Ethernet MAC address
explanations: Incorrect — returning only a root-server address is a referral, not completion of a recursive query.
Correct — a recursive resolver undertakes the lookup process and returns the requested result or an error to the client.
Incorrect — DNS resolution follows a structured hierarchy; it does not broadcast every query to all authoritative servers.
Incorrect — DNS resolves names to resource records such as IP addresses, not directly to Ethernet MAC addresses.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: IETF RFC 1034 and RFC 1035; DNS concepts and implementation.

questions.stem: Which condition is required for an XML document to be well-formed?
options: It may contain several unrelated root elements
Every element must have the same tag name
It must contain exactly one document element with properly nested start and end tags
Every element must have a DTD declaration
explanations: Incorrect — an XML document has exactly one document element; multiple top-level roots violate well-formedness.
Incorrect — elements may have different names according to the document vocabulary.
Correct — XML well-formedness requires one root document element and properly nested markup.
Incorrect — a DTD is not required merely for an XML document to be well-formed.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: W3C XML 1.0 Fifth Edition Recommendation; document well-formedness.

questions.stem: Which statement distinguishes a DOM parser from a SAX parser?
options: DOM builds an in-memory document tree, whereas SAX reports parsing events as the document is read
SAX always builds a complete editable tree before reporting anything
DOM is limited to XML files smaller than one kilobyte
Low cohesion and low coupling
explanations: Correct — DOM exposes a tree representation in memory, while SAX is event-driven and can process a stream incrementally.
Incorrect — SAX is event-driven and does not require building a complete tree.
Incorrect — DOM has no one-kilobyte size restriction; memory use is the practical concern.
Incorrect — low coupling is desirable, but low cohesion means a module groups unrelated responsibilities and is not the preferred design.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: W3C XML processing concepts; DOM and SAX parser documentation.

questions.stem: In the standard Java Servlet lifecycle, which sequence is correct for a servlet instance?
options: service(), init(), destroy()
destroy(), service(), init()
init(), service() for requests, then destroy()
init() for every request, then compile()
explanations: Incorrect — init() is called before request servicing, not after it.
Incorrect — destruction does not precede initialisation and service.
Correct — the container initialises the servlet, invokes service for requests, and calls destroy before removing the instance.
Incorrect — init() is not called for every request and servlet compilation is not a lifecycle callback.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: Jakarta Servlet specification; servlet lifecycle.

questions.stem: In a typical PHP session implementation, what does the browser usually store to let the server associate later requests with session data?
options: The complete server-side session array
A session identifier, commonly carried in a cookie
The server's database password
The PHP source code of the session handler
explanations: Incorrect — session data is normally stored server-side rather than sending the entire session array to the browser.
Correct — the browser typically returns a session identifier, often in a cookie, which lets the server locate session data.
Incorrect — credentials are not stored as the session identifier.
Incorrect — the browser does not receive the server-side PHP handler source code.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: PHP manual, Sessions; session identifiers and cookies.

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: Which C++ feature allows one function algorithm to be written for several compatible data types while retaining compile-time type checking?
options: Run-time reflection only
Function templates
Preprocessor text substitution only
Multiple inheritance
explanations: Incorrect — run-time reflection is not the standard mechanism for generic function definitions in C++.
Correct — function templates provide type-parameterised definitions instantiated for compatible argument types.
Incorrect — preprocessor substitution is textual and does not provide template type checking.
Incorrect — multiple inheritance concerns class inheritance, not generic function algorithms.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: ISO C++ standard; function templates and template argument deduction.

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: A Java reference of type Base refers to an object whose runtime class is Derived. Both classes define an overridden instance method show(). Which implementation is invoked by baseRef.show()?
options: Base.show() always, because the reference type controls overriding
Derived.show(), because overridden instance methods use dynamic dispatch
Both methods execute automatically
The compiler reports an error whenever a base reference refers to a derived object
explanations: Incorrect — the declared reference type controls compile-time accessibility, not the target of an overridden instance-method call.
Correct — Java selects the overridden instance method according to the runtime class of the object.
Incorrect — only the selected overriding implementation is invoked through this call.
Incorrect — assigning a derived instance to a compatible base reference is standard polymorphism.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: Java Language Specification 21; overriding and dynamic method lookup.

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: A Java class declares an abstract method export() and also declares a constructor that initialises a name field. Which statement is correct?
options: The constructor makes the class concrete automatically
An abstract class cannot have instance fields
The class may have the constructor and field, but it cannot be instantiated directly while abstract
The abstract method must be static
explanations: Incorrect — declaring a constructor does not implement the abstract method or make the class concrete.
Incorrect — abstract classes may declare and initialise instance fields.
Correct — an abstract class can hold state and define constructors for subclasses, but it cannot itself be instantiated.
Incorrect — abstract instance methods are not declared static.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: Java Language Specification 21; abstract classes and constructors.

questions.stem: In a transaction database of 30 baskets, itemset {tea, sugar} appears in 6 baskets. What is its support?
explanations: Incorrect — support is not the raw count expressed as a percentage of 100.
Incorrect — 15% would correspond to 4.5 baskets out of 30.
Correct — support({tea,sugar})=6/30=0.20, or 20%.
Incorrect — 30% would correspond to 9 of the 30 baskets.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques; association-rule support.

questions.stem: Among 10 transactions containing item A, 6 also contain item B. What is the confidence of the rule A→B?
explanations: Incorrect — 6 is the co-occurrence count, not 6% confidence.
Incorrect — 40% is the proportion containing A but not B.
Correct — confidence(A→B)=support(A∪B)/support(A)=6/10=60%.
Incorrect — 90% is not supported by the stated counts.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques; association-rule confidence.

questions.stem: A rule A→B has confidence 0.60, while item B occurs in 20% of all transactions. What is the lift of the rule?
explanations: Incorrect — 0.12 is the product of confidence and support(B), not the lift.
Incorrect — 0.80 is not the ratio of confidence to support(B).
Incorrect — 1.20 would require a different baseline support or confidence.
Correct — lift=confidence(A→B)/support(B)=0.60/0.20=3.00, indicating positive association relative to independence.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques; association-rule lift.

questions.stem: After assigning observations to clusters in K-means, how is each cluster centre updated in the standard algorithm?
options: As the arithmetic mean of the observations assigned to that cluster
As the observation farthest from every other point
As the most frequent categorical label, regardless of feature type
As a random point that is never recalculated
explanations: Correct — the K-means update step sets each centroid to the coordinate-wise mean of its assigned observations.
Incorrect — a farthest point is not the centroid update rule.
Incorrect — a mode may be used in other categorical clustering variants, not standard K-means on numeric vectors.
Incorrect — centroids are recalculated after assignment steps.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Standard K-means method; scikit-learn user guide, clustering.

questions.stem: For a decision-tree split, information gain is calculated as:
options: Weighted child entropy minus parent entropy
Parent entropy minus the weighted average entropy of the child nodes
The number of leaves multiplied by training accuracy
The Gini impurity of the root divided by the number of features
explanations: Incorrect — this reverses the usual reduction in uncertainty.
Correct — information gain is the parent entropy minus the weighted average entropy after the split.
Incorrect — leaf count and accuracy do not define information gain.
Incorrect — Gini impurity is a separate split criterion, not the stated entropy formula.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques; decision-tree induction.

questions.stem: In DBSCAN clustering, a point that is neither a core point nor density-reachable from any core point is classified as:
options: A centroid
A support vector
Noise
A mandatory cluster representative
explanations: Incorrect — DBSCAN does not calculate cluster centroids as part of its basic definition.
Incorrect — support vectors belong to support-vector machines.
Correct — points that cannot be assigned to a density-connected cluster are labelled noise or outliers.
Incorrect — DBSCAN has no requirement for a representative point in every cluster.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Ester et al., A Density-Based Algorithm for Discovering Clusters in Large Spatial Databases; DBSCAN.

questions.stem: The 'naive' assumption in a Naive Bayes classifier is that features are:
options: Mutually exclusive in the training data
Conditionally independent given the class label
Always normally distributed
Independent of the class label
explanations: Incorrect — features need not be mutually exclusive.
Correct — Naive Bayes assumes conditional independence of features given the class, simplifying likelihood computation.
Incorrect — Gaussian Naive Bayes uses a normal likelihood for continuous features, but that is not the general defining assumption.
Incorrect — features are used because they provide information about the class label.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Standard machine-learning texts; Naive Bayes conditional-independence assumption.
